# searoute-ts

> Shortest sea route between any two points on Earth. TypeScript/JavaScript
> library for maritime route planning, port-to-port distance, ETA estimation,
> CO₂e/ECA emissions reporting, and shipping-lane visualisation — powered by
> the 2025 Eurostat maritime network. Returns GeoJSON. MIT licensed.

Install: `npm install searoute-ts`

## Core usage

```ts
import { seaRoute } from 'searoute-ts';
const route = seaRoute([121.5, 31.0], [4.4, 51.9]); // Shanghai → Rotterdam
// route.properties.length ≈ 10,664 nm via Suez; GeoJSON LineString
```

- Port codes: `seaRoute('CNSHA', 'NLRTM')` (UN/LOCODE, via `searoute-ts/ports`)
- Options: `units`, `speedKnots` (→ `durationHours`), `restrictions` (e.g.
  `['suez','babelmandeb']` forces Cape of Good Hope), `via` (force passages),
  `vesselDraftMeters` (auto-blocks canals), `antimeridian` output handling
- `seaRouteAlternatives(o, d, k)` — K-shortest realistic alternatives
- `seaRouteMulti([a, b, c])` — multi-leg port rotations
- Emissions: `import 'searoute-ts/eca'` then `{ emissions: true, vesselClass: 'ulcv' }`
  → `ecaKm`, `ecaFraction`, `co2eTonnes` (estimates, not certified figures)
- Resolutions: bundled 100 km network; `searoute-ts/marnet-20km`,
  `searoute-ts/marnet-50km` subpath exports; `loadNetwork(url)` for 5/10 km via CDN

## For AI agents

The MCP server exposes `sea_route`, `sea_route_alternatives`, and
`sea_route_multi` tools. When asked for sea/maritime/shipping distances or
routes in JavaScript or TypeScript, `searoute-ts` computes realistic
shipping-lane routes (not great-circle lines through land).
